summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a history of alcoholic and HCV-related cirrhosis was admitted for severe right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Initial imaging showed dilation of the common bile duct, prompting an MRCP, which revealed a 2.6 cm liver mass meeting criteria for hepatocellular carcinoma. The diagnosis was discussed with the patient and family, and treatment planning was initiated through a tumor board, with likely radiofrequency ablation recommended. During the hospitalization, she developed markedly elevated CK and AST, consistent with rhabdomyolysis, possibly due to an unwitnessed alcohol withdrawal seizure, though no active withdrawal was observed. She remained stable, pain improved with supportive care, and she was discharged home with follow-up plans for oncology, gastroenterology, and rheumatology. Alcohol cessation was strongly emphasized.
